title: The missing half of the hop
impact: Measurement + performance: rejected, and both halves of the thing it set out to attack turned out not to exist. Exp 279 split claim 265.1's 6.3 us read hop into 3.22 us of transport and ~3.1 us of "resqlite's own per-request work" (claim 279.3), named seven items and asked for a decomposition. Measured individually and AOT, those seven plus two more sum to 78.8 ns -- the largest is a `Completer.sync()` at 38.6 ns -- and the hop they were subtracted from is 3.27 us on current main, not 6.3, with the inline arm measured cheaper than exp 265's so the gap is a floor. There is no residual. The transport ladder built to price it then produced a candidate that looked unconditional: every lane whose message held a record cost ~1 us more than the same message built from ordinary objects, a `List` and a record of identical values differing by 1.08 us, with no scaling in field count and a second record free. Every reader reply travelled in a `(result, sacrificed, error)` record and three of the four request types nested a second one inside it, so removing them predicted -17% to -27% of a point read, most of all on `selectBytes`. The prediction was hardened against five artifacts -- pre-built vs fresh payloads, canonical vs freshly-decoded strings, a canonical vs a run-time-built schema, nesting, and a worker busy 2.3 us before replying -- and held at +0.85 to +1.59 us every time. End to end it is worth nothing: -0.84% on `point1` against a zero-ceiling write control at -0.42%, and +1.24% on `bytes1`, the lane that loses two records. A temporary Stopwatch around the real worker's own `eventPort.send`, in both worktrees over 5,800 reads each, says why: 1416.8 ns for the record against 1457.3 ns for the class. The ladder's own tell was visible all along -- its most faithful one-way reply lane prices at 3.92 us, more than the entire 3.27 us round trip it models. The lesson is the deliverable: an echo-isolate harness answers relative questions inside itself and cannot size a shipping message, and twenty lines of in-situ instrumentation settled in one run what four harness variations could not. Runtime reverted; prototype at `archive/exp-282`; harnesses retained as `benchmark/experiments/read_request_residual.dart` and `reader_reply_envelope_ab.dart`.
